clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old female smoker presented with a 7-week history of fever, night sweats, joint pains, myalgia, nasal congestion, dizziness, and hearing impairment, following a prior hospitalization for presumed pneumonia. On readmission, she exhibited conjunctival injection secondary to episcleritis, a maculopapular rash, and nodular tender lesions. Initial investigations revealed normocytic normochromic anaemia, neutrophilic leucocytosis, and raised inflammatory markers, with negative blood/urine cultures and viral screens. Initial treatment with doxycycline, NSAIDs, and prochlorperazine was ineffective, and her hearing worsened. Audiometry confirmed bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. A skin biopsy of the lower limb rash showed perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate consistent with small- and medium-sized vessel vasculitis. Further autoimmune screens (ANA, ANCA, ASMA, RF, anti-CCP, complement levels) were negative, ruling out other systemic vasculitides. The patient subsequently developed all classical features of Cogan's syndrome, including audiovestibular and ocular involvement with vasculitis.

Other systemic vasculitides, such as granulomatosis with polyangiitis, were excluded by negative autoimmune screens (ANA, ANCA, ASMA, RF, anti-CCP, complement levels).
